# Offline PheWAS Installation on the Windows R 4.6.1 VM

## Goal

Install the `PheWAS` R package on the offline Windows VM. The packages are built
on the Mac, zipped, and carried across as pasted text, in the same way the
Pullmanager bundle is.

Three files next to this document do the work:

| File | Runs on | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `build_phewas_lib.R` | Mac | Works out what the VM is missing and assembles `Rlib/` |
| `phewas_transfer.py` | Mac, then VM | `pack` encodes `Rlib/` into text parts; `unpack` and `promote` rebuild and install it |
| `check_phewas_lib.R` | Mac, then VM | Checks every dependency is present at a sufficient version, and on the VM loads PheWAS |

`check_phewas_lib.R` travels inside the transfer. `phewas_transfer.py` has to be
pasted across once on its own.

## How it works

- **CRAN packages go across as Windows binaries.** CRAN publishes a zip for each
  package built for Windows R 4.6. Such a zip holds an installed package folder,
  and unzipping it is all `install.packages()` does with it on Windows. So a Mac
  can prepare a Windows library without building anything.
- **PheWAS goes across as source.** It is only on GitHub, so it has no Windows
  binary. It is pure R (it has no `src/` folder), so it installs from source on the
  VM without Rtools.
- **Only what the VM lacks is shipped.** The build compares PheWAS's full
  dependency tree with the VM's own package list. When this was written the
  answer was `CompQuadForm`, `meta` and `metabook`, plus PheWAS itself. `DT` and
  the other HTML packages are already on the VM.
- **Every paste is verified.** Each text part carries its own SHA-256 and the
  whole zip's. A bad paste is caught, and the error names the one part to copy
  again.
- **The live library is never half-updated.** `unpack` writes to `Rlib.new`. Only
  `promote` swaps it in, and only after `check_phewas_lib()` has passed there. The
  previous library is kept as `Rlib.old`.

## Constraints

- The VM runs R 4.6.1 x64. The build fetches binaries for Windows R 4.6
  explicitly, so the Mac's own R version does not decide what is shipped.
- Copy only public package files. Package names and versions are the only
  information that comes back from the VM.
- Nothing is loaded on the Mac, because Windows binaries cannot load there. The
  Mac check works from DESCRIPTION files alone, and the VM check then loads the
  packages for real.

## Part 0: Export the VM's package list

On the VM, in R:

```r
dir.create("C:/phewas_offline", showWarnings = FALSE)
ip <- installed.packages()
writeLines(paste(ip[, "Package"], ip[, "Version"]), "C:/phewas_offline/vm_packages.txt")
```

Bring `vm_packages.txt` back to the Mac as `~/phewas_transfer_build/vm_packages.txt`.
It holds one `name version` pair per line.

If text cannot come off the VM, skip this. The build then falls back to the
repo's inventory, `YAMLs/DSVM Plugins.yaml`. That file is out of date: it still
lists `parallel v4.5.1`, from before R was upgraded. So the check would be
judging against old versions.

## Part 1: Build the library on the Mac

This needs R (any recent version; 4.6 is best), `git` and `python3`. If `python3`
is missing, `xcode-select --install` provides it.

### 1. Build `Rlib/`

In Terminal, from the repo root:

```bash
Rscript QMDs/sideproject-phewas/build_phewas_lib.R
```

It works in `~/phewas_transfer_build`, creating that folder if needed, and starts
afresh on every run. It:

1. clones PheWAS from GitHub and builds a source tarball of it;
2. finds PheWAS's dependencies, recursively, from CRAN's Windows R 4.6 index;
3. drops base R and everything the VM already has;
4. downloads the rest as Windows binaries and unzips them into `Rlib/`;
5. adds the PheWAS tarball and `check_phewas_lib.R`;
6. runs the Mac-side check.

`R CMD build` warns that PheWAS now depends on R >= 3.5.0. That is expected and
harmless. The run ends with `Shipping as Windows binaries: …`, then either
`OK: … dependencies satisfied` followed by the pack command, or a list of
problems:

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| `X needs Y >= a, but b is available` | The VM's copy of `Y` is too old. Add `"Y"` to `extra` at the top of `build_phewas_lib.R` and rerun. The shipped copy then shadows the VM's for sessions that use this library. |
| `X needs Y, which is missing` | `Y` is missing from the VM's list. Investigate before continuing. |
| `Not on CRAN for Windows R 4.6: …` | A dependency has no Windows binary. Investigate before continuing. |
| `X is not a Windows build` | Something other than a Windows binary got into `Rlib/`. Rerun the script. |

Do not pack until the check says `OK`.

### 2. Pack it into text parts

From the repo root:

```bash
python3 QMDs/sideproject-phewas/phewas_transfer.py pack \
  ~/phewas_transfer_build/Rlib ~/phewas_transfer_build/parts
```

It prints the number of parts, the zip size and its SHA-256. With the current
contents that is about 3.6 MB of zip in five parts of about 1 MB each. If the
channel into the VM takes less at a time, add `--lines-per-part 6500` for
roughly 500 KB parts.

Each part looks like this:

```text
# PHEWAS-TRANSFER v1 part 1/5
# zip-sha256: <64 hex> zip-bytes: <n>
# part-sha256: <64 hex>
<base64, 76 characters a line>
# END part 1/5
```

## Part 2: Rebuild on the VM

### 1. Put the transfer script on the VM (first time only)

Paste the contents of `phewas_transfer.py` into `C:\phewas_offline\phewas_transfer.py`.
It needs only the Python standard library. Later transfers reuse it unless it
changes.

### 2. Paste the parts

Paste each part into its own file in `C:\phewas_offline\parts\`, such as
`part01.txt`. The file names do not matter; the headers carry the order. Putting
several parts in one file also works.

Keep each paste exactly as copied, header and `END` line included. Blank lines,
Windows line endings and a Notepad byte-order mark are all tolerated. Anything
else in the file is refused. Empty the folder before starting a new transfer.

### 3. Verify and unpack

```powershell
python C:\phewas_offline\phewas_transfer.py unpack C:\phewas_offline\parts C:\phewas_offline\Rlib
```

This reports `Verified N part(s)` and the packages it extracted into
`C:\phewas_offline\Rlib.new`. On failure it names what to do:

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `part N does not match its hash -- re-copy part N` | That paste was altered. Copy that one part again. |
| `part N has no matching END line -- the paste was cut short` | The paste was truncated. Copy that one part again. |
| `Missing part(s) [...]` / `Part N appears twice` | Add or remove files so there is exactly one copy of each part. |
| `The parts come from different builds` | Parts from an older pack are mixed in. Empty the folder and paste one pack's parts. |
| `expected a part header` | Extra text was pasted before a part. Delete it. |

### 4. Install PheWAS from source, then check

In a fresh R session on the VM:

```r
lib <- "C:/phewas_offline/Rlib.new"
.libPaths(c(lib, .libPaths()))

install.packages(list.files(lib, "\\.tar\\.gz$", full.names = TRUE),
                 lib = lib, repos = NULL, type = "source")

source(file.path(lib, "check_phewas_lib.R"))
check_phewas_lib(lib)
```

The check confirms that every package was built for R 4.6 and that each
dependency is present at a sufficient version. It then loads PheWAS. On success it
prints `OK: … loaded and marked as checked` and leaves a `.check-passed` marker,
which `promote` requires.

### 5. Restart R, then promote

Windows cannot move a folder whose DLLs an R session has loaded. So quit R (in
RStudio, *Session → Restart R*, or close it), then:

```powershell
python C:\phewas_offline\phewas_transfer.py promote C:\phewas_offline\Rlib
```

`C:\phewas_offline\Rlib` is now the checked library, and any earlier one is kept
as `Rlib.old`. If Windows still refuses, close every R session and run `promote`
again. A failed promote puts the previous library back.

## Part 3: Use the library

At the top of every script that uses PheWAS:

```r
phewas_library <- "C:/phewas_offline/Rlib"
stopifnot(dir.exists(phewas_library))
.libPaths(c(phewas_library, .libPaths()))

library(PheWAS)
```

`library(PheWAS)` loads `meta`, `metabook` and `CompQuadForm` as it needs them.
To add the library to every session automatically, put the `.libPaths()` line in
`.Rprofile`, but only after `promote` has succeeded.

## Part 4: Final test

```r
packageVersion("PheWAS")
data(package = "PheWAS")$results[, "Item"]
head(PheWAS::pheinfo)
```

If this runs without error, PheWAS works offline.

## Notes

- **HTML output.** PheWAS imports `DT`, an HTML-table package, so `DT` has to be
  installed, and it already is on the VM. Loading it opens nothing. Only PheWAS's
  interactive-table output would try to show HTML. The statistics and the
  ggplot2 plots do not need it.
- **Updating.** Rerun Parts 1 and 2. `unpack` replaces any earlier `Rlib.new`, and
  `promote` replaces the previous `Rlib.old`.
- **Why not the repo's bundle format?** `scripts/bundle_extractor.py` carries text
  source files as commented lines, and cannot carry a binary zip. This transfer
  borrows its safeguards instead: hashes embedded in the payload, a staged
  extraction swapped in only after checks pass, refusal of unsafe paths in the
  zip, and a check that ships with the payload so the VM can verify it.
- Base64 makes the text about a third larger than the zip.
